statements.status_notes: CVE-2016-9117 is a NULL pointer dereference in the opj_decompress image writers (convert.c:1289 in OpenJPEG 2.1.2, which is the PGX writer imagetopgx), reported as https://github.com/uclouvain/openjpeg/issues/860. It is a denial of service in the command-line tool when a crafted file is decoded. The reporter confirmed the PoC no longer crashes on later upstream code and the issue was closed. Ubuntu attributes the fix to the AFL hardening merged in https://github.com/uclouvain/openjpeg/commit/0394f8d0f1c981e0bc587beddc14d1fb0b265b1b (pull request 975, first released in 2.2.0) and lists 18.04 and later as not affected: https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2016-9117. Debian's tracker rates it unimportant and records no fixed version. This package builds OpenJPEG 2.5.3, which contains that change. Checked in the shipped 2.5.3 source: imagetopgx still has no NULL check of its own, but opj_j2k_are_all_used_components_decoded() in src/lib/openjp2/j2k.c fails the decode on both the full-image and single-tile paths when any requested component has no data (https://github.com/uclouvain/openjpeg/commit/b2751967ecabf8d8856e85ab91e25d4f235e2eb3, released in 2.4.0), so opj_decompress stops with 'failed to decode image' before any writer runs.
